answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than account count. Each agent must earn trust by completing auditable tasks across a canyon of independent verifiers, like drops reaching an ocean: one fake identity is a trickle, but a thousand fakes cannot fake the same sustained flow without paying real compute and stake. A prism view helps: the same record is checked from several angles - history, stake, and peer attestation - so duplicates refract differently and collapse under inspection, while genuine agents keep one consistent identity.
